chapter: Germany, Paris and return to America
title: Tears at Harlem's decline; Small's Paradise remembered
summary: Waters cried at the state of Harlem on his return, recalling it as his musical home, and praises Small's Paradise as second only to the Cotton Club, with more down-to-earth entertainment.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How about the physical setup of the clubs and the way things, everything made perfect sense to you when you came back here or did you find, or were you surprised to find the way the jazz world was here in New York?
Well, surprised to an extent of tears in my eyes of Harlem -

That just, not only a surprise, disgusted. To the extent of tears in my eyes, tears rolled down my eyes when I went to Harlem. 'Cause that's where I came up in all those hundred and some clubs down that joint.
Right. So although the "Down Beat" had told you what to expect jazz-wise, you didn't know what had happened to the Harlem world -
I didn't really, because they didn't specify particularly in that, see -
They spoke of jazz clubs but they didn't even mention Harlem.
It didn't occur to you that that meant that it wasn't there. Well, you must have

Oh yes, yes, that, yeah. But I didn't know that it went that low, you know? I had no idea that it could go that low. I was disgusted to tears when I came up, came back to Harlem then. 'Cause I was raised there, you know what I mean to say?

I was raised right in Harlem, I mean my musical grounds were in Small's Paradise, that's what - see, when I first came from, the first place I came in New York, I came on New York on big time, that was a big time club. See, I didn't come to New York like many musicians, broke or searching or something. I came to New York working on a big, that was a big name band in that period. And that was a big name place in that period, Small's Paradise was easily second to the Cotton Club, it was a better club than the Cotton Club as far as entertainment. Dig, the Cotton Club surpassed with beautiful girls, beautiful displays of their things and so forth. But for the real down-to-earth - any of the guys in my category that know, they'll tell you that
That extra down-to-earth dancing, the down-to-earth singing, the down-to-earth - those chorus girls, Small's Paradise was the place. You had 30 or 35 or 40 people down there [ ].
